paragraphs.source_en:
He who taught man to vanquish whatsoever
Can be between the cradle and the grave
Crowned him the King of Life. Oh, vain endeavour!
 If on his own high will, a willing slave
He has enthroned the oppression and the oppressor.

happy’; 1824 clarifies the lines so they mean: ‘all the things we dream of being: happy, high, majestic’.
 Hunt MS punctuation leaves room for the sense suggested by cancelled Nbk 6 wording that our dreams
of happiness, like high thoughts, help create happiness for us. majestical] Kelvin Everest points out the

very social structure that obstructs the realization of his ideals’ (Shelley Revalued 74). Cp. Lines Written
among the Euganean Hills 73: ‘The sun’s uprise majestical’.
 Where . . . mind?] Echoing Byron in Childe Harold iv 37–43: ‘The beings of the mind are not of
clay;/Essentially immortal, they create/And multiply in us a brighter ray/And more beloved existence’.
